title: Looking for the best all time college coaches? See here!

source.pdf_page_offset_note: Physical pages 1-2 are the summary and execution-flow sheets; later printed page labels differ, so this record uses physical-page citations.

notes: All 44 UTF-8 physical-page files were read sequentially, with the summary sheet and introduction preceding the later models.
Eight JPEG contact-sheet proxies of 42,333-167,386 bytes covered every physical page one at a time; ten focused JPEG crops of 95,756-213,965 bytes checked formula and plot fidelity.
No original full-page PNG or multi-image result entered model transport; originals remain on disk as coordinate authority.
No blank, clipped, overlapping, or missing page was found. Physical page 44 contains only the terminal appendix row by source design.

inputs: male and female college coach records
decisions: how era and gender adjustments alter fields
whether transfer and robustness claims are warranted

section_map.summary: The summary sheet and execution flow state the best-coach decision, PCA factor compression, cosine ranking, time and gender adjustments, extension, sensitivity, and robustness claims.
The illustrated problem framing, question list, and contents translate a broad all-time coach comparison into factor selection, ranking, adjustment, extension, and stability work.
The introduction frames college-coach ranking as a multi-factor comparison, identifies the intended sports and genders, and announces an evaluation-system route.
The assumptions table declares representativeness, data reliability, and the role of time horizon and gender in the later adjustment models.
The paper lists twelve coach factors, standardizes them, builds a correlation matrix, extracts principal components, and interprets ability, college influence, and social influence.
The ranking model defines an ideal coach, uses cosine similarity and an adjusted form, clusters sixty coaches by Euclidean single linkage, then reports the baseline list.
The initial top-ten table is used to introduce timeline and gender differences as reasons to modify the basic similarity ranking.
The time-line module regresses active NCAA coaches on year, converts the relation into a career-average difficulty coefficient, caps the giant effect, adjusts Google searches, and reranks.
The gender module uses one-way ANOVA to select differing factors, then rescales female wins by data whitening before a final basketball ranking.
A factor pool maps shared and sport-specific fields before football, softball, baseball, and Chinese basketball coach ranking demonstrations.
Photo-backed basketball, football, and baseball tables and a U.S. regional map turn the ranking outputs into a decision-facing presentation.
The source compares rankings before and after adjustments, adds unspecified noise to the first fifteen coaches, and uses limited order stability as stability and robustness evidence.
The closing evaluation names credibility, accessibility, self-improvement, reliability, and adaptability, then admits narrow-factor and lower-ability ranking limits.
The conclusion restates the similarity, timeline, gender, transfer, and robustness claims; the references expose web and method dependencies without frozen computational inputs.
The appendix supplies original and modified rows for the sixty basketball coaches, making several transformations inspectable while leaving their full pipeline and provenance incomplete.

assumptions.summary: The chosen factors are assumed to represent coach ability and the selected coaches to represent the intended leading pool.
Collected statistics and Google-search counts are assumed reliable enough for the calculations.
Timeline horizon and gender are assumed to create ranking differences that can be addressed by the named adjustments.
The number of active NCAA coaches is assumed proportional to coaching difficulty.
The fitted active-coach relation is assumed adequate for all career years used in the integral.
The giant-effect cap of 1.5 is chosen as a minor rather than dominant correction without a calibration criterion.
One-way ANOVA at alpha 0.05 is assumed appropriate for each factor comparison.
Matching a selected variance is assumed to remove enough gender influence for reranking.
The factor pool is assumed sufficiently portable across sports and countries after field selection.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: Twelve factors include tenure, NCAA tenure, wins, losses, games, winning rate, teams, Final Fours, NCAA championships, conference championships, Google searches, and awards.
The ideal coach vector combines factor-wise maxima from the sixty coach rows.
Table 5 assigns sixty coaches to clusters before the first-group ranking calculation.
The timeline regression uses active NCAA coaches from 1942 to 2013 but does not ship the source series.
Career start and stop years are used to integrate a coach-specific difficulty coefficient.
Table 9 lists p values for factor comparisons between thirty male and thirty female coaches.
Table 10 reports male and female win standard deviations and variances before whitening.
Tables 13-15 provide football, softball, and baseball top-five outputs but not their complete source rosters.
Appendix rows provide original basketball records, and later pages show modified wins, games, and winning rates.

models.summary: Declare the sixty-coach basketball sample and twelve candidate factors before evaluation.
Standardize twelve factors, construct correlations, retain components, and interpret their loadings.
Construct the ideal factor vector and score every coach by cosine similarity.
Center factor values, use Euclidean single linkage, and select the best cluster for ranking.
Use the baseline top ten to identify timeline and gender comparability problems.
Regress active coaches on time and translate the result to a career-average capped difficulty coefficient.
Normalize coaching start year and divide search counts by the social-influence coefficient.
Test male and female factor differences before selecting fields for adjustment.
Rescale affected female factor values and verify the displayed before/after variance.
Map common and sport-specific factors before producing receiving-domain coach lists.
Present basketball, football, baseball, and regional outputs with named coaches and selected statistics.
Compare adjusted rankings and add noise to the first fifteen coach records before comparing top places.

dependency_graph.handoff: Declared coach records and twelve factor columns enter standardization and PCA.
The chosen factor system supplies the ideal vector and coach comparison dimensions.
The cosine limitation motivates centering and cluster-based eligibility.
The initial rank reveals timeline and gender variables that are not yet adjusted.
Timeline data and career dates enter the active-coach regression and career average.
Start year is reused to normalize the Google-search social-influence field.
The timeline-adjusted coach table is the input on which gender differences are tested.
ANOVA-selected factors receive the variance-matching transformation.
The adjusted basketball interface is generalized through the factor pool.
Receiving-domain ranks are displayed as tables and regional context.
The reported lists provide before/after outputs for adjustment and noise comparison.

verification.summary: Table 2 reports eigenvalues and cumulative contribution rates for all twelve principal components.
verification.strength: The retained component calculation is visible.
verification.limitation: Factor measurement and component-retention criterion are not independently validated.

verification.summary: Table 3 displays factor loadings for Z1, Z2, and Z3.
verification.strength: The component labels can be checked against displayed loadings.
verification.limitation: Labels remain interpretive and Google-search provenance is absent.

verification.summary: Table 5 displays cluster membership for the sixty coach records.
verification.strength: The selected cluster step is visible.
verification.limitation: The number of clusters and cut criterion are not justified.

verification.summary: Tables 7 and 8 compare the top ten before and after the timeline adjustment.
verification.strength: The effect of the stated correction is inspectable.
verification.limitation: Near-unchanged order does not validate the difficulty or search mechanism.

verification.summary: Table 9 reports ANOVA p values for factor differences.
verification.strength: The selected significance mechanism is displayed.
verification.limitation: Definitions, degrees of freedom, multiple testing, and raw factor distributions are incomplete.

verification.summary: Table 11 compares male and female win variance after the whitening transformation.
verification.strength: The reported variance target can be compared.
verification.limitation: A variance match is not evidence of comparability or fairness.

verification.summary: Tables 13-15 show top-five lists in three receiving sports.
verification.limitation: No independent receiving-sport validation or data archive is supplied.

verification.summary: Table 20 compares rank order before and after combined adjustments.
verification.strength: Several top positions can be checked.
verification.limitation: The changed settings, data versions, and acceptance threshold are not fully specified.

verification.summary: Table 22 compares the noisy and original lists after noise is added to the first fifteen coaches.
verification.strength: A limited top-rank response is shown.
verification.limitation: Noise distribution, magnitude, seed, repetitions, and full-rank effect are absent.

results_trace.summary: The source names Z1 coach ability, Z2 college influence, and Z3 social influence after inspecting the component matrix.
The initial cosine ranking lists John Wooden first, followed by Geno Auriemma and Pat Summitt.
Timeline adjustment replaces John Thompson with Billy Donovan in the displayed top ten while retaining the leading nine places.
After gender and timeline adjustment, Tara VanDerveer appears ninth and Tom Izzo tenth in the displayed top ten.
The transfer tables rank Bear Bryant first in football and Sue Enquist first in softball; Table 15 is labeled softball despite baseball names.
The country extension reports a Chinese basketball coach top five after an unspecified factor-pool update.
The final basketball presentation begins with John Wooden, Geno Auriemma, Pat Summitt, Dean Smith, and Mike Krzyzewski.
The noise comparison keeps John Wooden, Geno Auriemma, and Pat Summitt as the displayed first three after perturbation.

contributions.summary: Twelve explicit coach factors create a visible measurement interface.
The component matrix exposes the basis for three named factor groupings.
The direction-only cosine counterexample motivates a stated scale-aware adjustment.
Timeline correction is expressed as regression, career aggregation, and a capped multiplier rather than an undocumented bonus.
ANOVA is used as a declared selection gate before gender transformation.
The factor pool makes shared and sport-specific fields visible before transfer.
The paper at least displays a noisy-input comparison rather than asserting stability with no perturbation evidence.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: The summary presents a complete route from factor analysis through adjustment and transfer, without proving that the route itself caused award recognition.
The source openly demonstrates cosine's scale limitation before proposing an adjustment, which improves inspectability without validating the corrected rank.
The factor-pool diagram makes transfer assumptions visible before result tables, without proving cross-sport equivalence.

weaknesses.summary: The displayed correlation denominator's second sum is indexed i=1..n while the term uses x_kj, leaving a visible index mismatch.
The cumulative contribution numerator visibly uses an inconsistent upper index, so the retained-component formula needs a typed reconstruction before implementation.
The printed cosine formula continues below the page region and the text states eleven standardized dimensions despite later defining a twelve-factor vector.
The standard-deviation summand visibly uses xbar_ij while the mean is defined as xbar_j, a subscript inconsistency.
The printed general Minkowski expression omits absolute values and the merge line labels D_kr squared while the right side is an unsquared minimum distance.
The source first states D(t)=kA(t) but then prints D(t)=(0.734t-1421.8)/k, so the role of k and units are contradictory.
The giant-effect piecewise rule is visually ambiguous and its 0.5 threshold and 1.5 cap are not calibrated or sensitivity-tested.
The ANOVA notation defines N as the two coach kinds while using N-I degrees of freedom, and the printed grand-mean notation is inconsistent.
The narrative says losses have p>alpha although Table 9 prints L=0.004, which is below 0.05.
The source's printed whitening ratio must be reconciled with the intended variance target before using the formula; a variance claim alone does not establish fair comparison.
Table 15 is titled Softball Coach Ranking but lists baseball names and repeats Ron Fraser, so the transfer output cannot be accepted without source reconciliation.
The noise test gives no distribution, scale, random seed, repetitions, or full-order effect and visually relies on overlapping red and blue marks.
No frozen raw data, source snapshots, factor definitions, transformation code, clustering settings, regression data, ANOVA output, seeds, or independent validation package is supplied.

independent_extensions.summary: Publish a versioned data dictionary for all twelve factors, including source, collection date, unit, direction, missingness, and each coach identifier.
Implement and test PCA equations with unambiguous summation indices, a justified retention rule, sign conventions, and reproducible component labels.
Compare cosine, scale-aware distances, and rank-aggregation alternatives using a predeclared fairness and predictive criterion.
Specify linkage, cluster-count selection, distance scaling, and cluster stability resampling before selecting the rank-eligible group.
Fit and publish a timeline model with units, residual diagnostics, confidence intervals, sensitivity to historical data definition, and a causal boundary.
Use a documented ANOVA or regression design with correct degrees of freedom, multiplicity handling, effect sizes, diagnostics, and explicitly justified transformation targets.
Require sport-specific field maps, normalized score contracts, complete receiving rosters, and held-out comparators before treating transfer lists as validated.
Run seeded replicated perturbations across data, parameters, clustering, timeline, and transformation choices; report full-rank distributions and failure cases.
Release raw and derived tables, source snapshots, code, environment lock, model configuration, regression and ANOVA outputs, and an end-to-end reproduction log.
